hero.headline: FBI arrests suspects in alleged plot to attack White House UFC event with explosive drones
hero.body:
Federal law enforcement officials have disrupted an alleged plot to attack a UFC event at the White House using guns and explosive-laden drones, with multiple arrests made across several states.

According to a law enforcement official, five people were arrested in a multi-state operation involving suspects from Ohio, Missouri, and California. FBI Director Kash Patel confirmed that the agency had disrupted the planned attack before any harm could occur.

Court filings that were recently unsealed reveal that the group allegedly expressed grievances about corruption, references to the Epstein files, and data centres. The specifics of how these concerns connected to the alleged plot remain part of the ongoing investigation.

The UFC cage fighting event was scheduled to take place at the White House on Sunday. The arrests represent the latest in a series of security threats targeting high-profile events at the executive mansion. The choice of venue drew significant attention given that the president hosted the mixed martial arts organization at the White House.

Federal authorities have not yet released the identities of all suspects or detailed what specific charges each person faces. Officials also have not disclosed the full extent of how they learned about the alleged plot or how advanced the planning had progressed before the arrests took place. The investigation involved coordination among multiple federal agencies working to assess the threat level and prevent a potential attack.

The thwarted plot highlights growing concerns about drone-related threats to government facilities and public events. In recent years, the increased accessibility of drone technology has prompted security officials to develop new protocols and monitoring systems. The Secret Service and other protective agencies maintain extensive security measures for events on White House grounds, including airspace restrictions and screening procedures for attendees.

Security at the White House has become increasingly complex as new potential threats emerge. Event organizers and law enforcement must balance public access with comprehensive safety measures. The use of drones equipped with explosives represents a relatively modern security challenge that protective agencies have had to address with updated technology and strategies.

The arrests demonstrate federal law enforcement's commitment to identifying and disrupting potential threats before they materialize. Coordination between agencies across state lines proved essential in this case, as suspects were located in multiple regions. The investigation remains ongoing, with additional details likely to emerge as the legal process moves forward.

The incident adds to a growing list of security incidents and threats that have required federal intervention at the White House and other government facilities. As threats continue to evolve, security protocols will likely continue to adapt to address emerging risks.

cards.headline: Iran Says Deal to End War With US Requires Israeli Withdrawal From Lebanon
cards.teaser: Iran stated Tuesday that its agreement to end the war with the United States includes a requirement for Israel to withdraw its forces from Lebanon.
cards.body:
Iran stated Tuesday that its agreement to end the war with the United States requires Israel to withdraw from Lebanon. Iran's foreign minister confirmed that new talks on nuclear arms and sanctions relief will begin Friday, immediately following the signing of an initial agreement.

President Trump expressed hope at the G7 summit about concluding the conflict. However, the ceasefire remains fragile, with few Lebanese residents returning to southern Lebanon despite the truce. France, Britain, and other nations announced plans to send ships, minesweepers, and other vessels to the Strait of Hormuz to secure the waterway once fighting ends.

cards.headline: European Union Approves Trade Deal With US After Year of Negotiations
cards.teaser: The agreement struck between President Trump and EU leaders in Scotland moves toward final approval.
cards.body:
European Union lawmakers gave final approval to a trade deal with the United States on Tuesday, nearly a year after the agreement was initially proposed. The deal faced a July 4 deadline, as the US had threatened to raise tariffs if it wasn't sanctioned by that date.

The European Parliament approved the agreement with two main conditions. The tariff deal was originally struck between President Trump and EU officials in Turnberry, Scotland last July.

cards.headline: Trump at G7 Summit Says Ukraine War Has No Impact on United States
cards.teaser: The president's remarks underscored divisions among allies gathered for the annual meeting.
cards.body:
President Trump arrived at the G7 summit in France, where he touted a preliminary agreement with Iran. The deal created an unexpectedly lighter atmosphere at the gathering, with French President Emmanuel Macron congratulating Trump on the nuclear accord.

However, Trump's comments that the Ukraine war has no impact on the United States underscored divisions among allied nations. G7 allies have been pushing to keep Ukraine central to the summit's agenda as the conflict continues, but the Iran agreement has shifted focus away from the war.

cards.headline: Trump shifts oversight of special education and civil rights out of Education Department
cards.teaser: The president moved special education programs to Health and Human Services and civil rights enforcement to the Justice Department.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump has transferred oversight of special education programs to the Department of Health and Human Services and moved civil rights enforcement to the Justice Department. These shifts remove significant functions from the Education Department, which Trump has pledged to eliminate.

The reorganization represents a substantial reduction in the Education Department's scope and authority. Special education programs serving millions of students with disabilities now fall under HHS oversight, while civil rights enforcement, including school discrimination investigations, shifts to the Justice Department. The changes align with Trump's stated goal of dismantling the federal education agency.

cards.headline: Senate Judiciary schedules confirmation hearing for attorney general nominee Todd Blanche
cards.teaser: The Senate Judiciary Committee set a confirmation hearing for Todd Blanche, nominated for attorney general.
cards.body:
The Senate Judiciary Committee scheduled a confirmation hearing for Todd Blanche, President Trump's nominee for attorney general. The hearing represents a key step in the confirmation process for the top Justice Department position.

Supporters hope Blanche can be confirmed before the August recess. The timeline would allow the nominee to take office before Congress breaks for its summer break.

cards.headline: Trump administration orders Anthropic to block foreign access to AI models
cards.teaser: The Trump administration issued an export control order to artificial intelligence company Anthropic, requiring it to block foreign nationals from accessing its.
cards.body:
Anthropic will disable its most advanced AI models, Fable 5 and Mythos 5, after receiving an export control directive from the U.S. government. The order requires the company to suspend access for all foreign nationals, citing national security concerns. Anthropic said it was not provided specific details about the security threat.

The government believes the models' safeguards can be bypassed and used to identify software vulnerabilities. AI researchers and cybersecurity leaders have raised concerns that this precedent could discourage American companies from developing defensive security tools, potentially weakening U.S. cyber defenses.

hero.headline: France and Britain to Send Ships to Strait of Hormuz as Iran Fighting Ends
hero.teaser: A coalition led by Britain and France will deploy minesweepers and other vessels to secure the strategic waterway.
hero.body:
France, Britain, and other countries announced Tuesday they will send naval vessels to the Strait of Hormuz following the end of fighting between the United States and Iran. The coalition has been preparing for months to deploy minesweepers and other ships to secure the strait.

The planned deployment comes as a preliminary ceasefire agreement takes shape. The coalition's mission will focus on ensuring safe passage through the strategic waterway, which serves as a vital route for global oil shipments.

cards.headline: Iran Says Deal to End War With US Requires Israeli Withdrawal From Lebanon
cards.teaser: Iran stated Tuesday that its agreement to end the war with the United States includes a requirement for Israel to withdraw its forces from Lebanon.
cards.body:
Iran stated Tuesday that its agreement to end the war with the United States requires Israel to withdraw from Lebanon. Iran's foreign minister confirmed that new talks on nuclear arms and sanctions relief will begin Friday, immediately following the signing of an initial agreement.

President Trump expressed hope at the G7 summit about concluding the conflict. However, the ceasefire remains fragile, with few Lebanese residents returning to southern Lebanon despite the truce. France, Britain, and other nations announced plans to send ships, minesweepers, and other vessels to the Strait of Hormuz to secure the waterway once fighting ends.

cards.teaser: The agreement struck between President Trump and EU leaders in Scotland moves toward final approval.
cards.body:
European Union lawmakers gave final approval to a trade deal with the United States on Tuesday, nearly a year after the agreement was initially proposed. The deal faced a July 4 deadline, as the US had threatened to raise tariffs if it wasn't sanctioned by that date.

The European Parliament approved the agreement with two main conditions. The tariff deal was originally struck between President Trump and EU officials in Turnberry, Scotland last July.

cards.headline: UK Investigates Reports Russian Warship Fired Warning Shots Near Yacht
cards.teaser: A yacht reportedly drifted toward a Russian frigate operating in the English Channel.
cards.body:
Britain's Defense Ministry is investigating reports that a Russian frigate fired warning shots near a UK-registered yacht in the English Channel. The incident involved the Admiral Grigorovich, a Russian naval vessel that has been operating in the Channel. The yacht had drifted toward the warship in the incident.

The shooting occurred in international waters where the Russian frigate was conducting operations.

cards.headline: Trump at G7 Summit Says Ukraine War Has No Impact on United States
cards.teaser: The president's remarks underscored divisions among allies gathered for the annual meeting.
cards.body:
President Trump arrived at the G7 summit in France, where he touted a preliminary agreement with Iran. The deal created an unexpectedly lighter atmosphere at the gathering, with French President Emmanuel Macron congratulating Trump on the nuclear accord.

However, Trump's comments that the Ukraine war has no impact on the United States underscored divisions among allied nations. G7 allies have been pushing to keep Ukraine central to the summit's agenda as the conflict continues, but the Iran agreement has shifted focus away from the war.

cards.headline: Russian Artist and Putin Critic Shot Dead in Poland
cards.teaser: Robert Kuzovkov was known for his caricatures of politicians including Vladimir Putin.
cards.body:
Robert Kuzovkov, a Russian artist known by the pseudonym Semyon Skrepetsky, has been shot dead in Poland. He was recognized for his political caricatures, particularly those depicting Vladimir Putin and other politicians.

Kuzovkov's artistic work established him as a vocal critic of the Russian government among dissident artists. Polish authorities are investigating the incident.

cards.headline: UK Defence Chief Warns Forces Face Cuts Without Additional Funding
cards.teaser: Britain's top military officer said operations would need to be scaled back without more spending.
cards.body:
Britain's defence chief has cautioned that military operations will be scaled back without increased government funding. The warning highlights growing concerns about budget constraints affecting the armed forces' capabilities across the Army, Navy, and Royal Air Force.

The alert comes amid ongoing pressure to sustain the UK's military commitments. Former Defence Secretary John Healey emphasized the urgency of the situation, noting that adversaries "do not follow timetables set by the Treasury," underscoring the unpredictable nature of security threats.

cards.headline: Tropical storm watch issued for Texas as Gulf Coast disturbance threatens flooding
cards.teaser: A tropical disturbance in the Gulf of Mexico could bring heavy rain and flooding to parts of Texas and the South.
cards.body:
Weather forecasters issued a tropical storm watch for parts of Texas as a waterlogged tropical disturbance in the Gulf of Mexico moves toward the coast. The system, designated Potential Tropical Cyclone One, could become the first named storm of the Atlantic hurricane season.

The disturbance threatens to bring heavy rainfall and flooding to the Gulf Coast region. Forecasters warned that the storm system could produce significant rain accumulation across Texas and other southern states. Millions of residents in the path of the storm face potential impacts from flooding and tropical storm conditions.

cards.headline: Trump shifts oversight of special education and civil rights out of Education Department
cards.teaser: The president moved special education programs to Health and Human Services and civil rights enforcement to the Justice Department.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump has transferred oversight of special education programs to the Department of Health and Human Services and moved civil rights enforcement to the Justice Department. These shifts remove significant functions from the Education Department, which Trump has pledged to eliminate.

The reorganization represents a substantial reduction in the Education Department's scope and authority. Special education programs serving millions of students with disabilities now fall under HHS oversight, while civil rights enforcement, including school discrimination investigations, shifts to the Justice Department. The changes align with Trump's stated goal of dismantling the federal education agency.

cards.headline: US adopts Iranian smuggling tactics to move oil out of Persian Gulf
cards.teaser: The United States is using methods previously employed by Iranian smugglers to transport oil from the Gulf region.
cards.body:
The United States has adopted smuggling tactics previously used by Iran to move oil out of the Persian Gulf, according to a report. The methods mirror techniques Iranian operators developed to evade sanctions and international monitoring of their oil shipments.

The development comes as President Trump announced an agreement with Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Trump claimed the waterway would be permanently toll-free under the deal and that it would be fully operational by Friday. However, most commercial shipping vessels have remained in place despite the announcement, with ship operators waiting for clearer confirmation of safe passage through the strategic waterway.

cards.headline: Algae returns to National Mall reflecting pool after $14 million renovation
cards.teaser: Workers dumped hydrogen peroxide into the reflecting pool to combat algae growth that reappeared after Trump's flag-themed renovation.
cards.body:
A $14.2 million renovation of the Lincoln Memorial reflecting pool has failed to maintain its intended appearance. Green algae have returned to the water despite the costly project, which was designed to create a patriotic display.

The renovation was commissioned to transform the pool into a red, white, and blue American flag pattern. National Park Service crews have attempted to combat the algae growth using hydrogen peroxide treatments, but the water has turned green again following warm weather.

cards.headline: SpaceX surpasses Amazon to become world's fifth most valuable company
cards.teaser: Elon Musk's rocket company overtook Amazon in market value following a surge in its share price.
cards.body:
SpaceX has become the world's fifth most valuable company, surpassing Amazon after a rise in the rocket company's share price. Elon Musk's space exploration and satellite firm now ranks above the retail and media giant in total market valuation.

The valuation increase reflects growing investor confidence in SpaceX's business operations, which include launching satellites, resupplying the International Space Station, and developing rockets for deep space missions. The company has expanded its commercial satellite internet service and continues to secure contracts for government and private sector launches.

cards.headline: Russian warship fires warning shots at UK-registered yacht in English Channel
cards.teaser: A Russian frigate fired warning shots after a British yacht drifted toward the vessel operating in the Channel.
cards.body:
A Russian frigate, the Admiral Grigorovich, fired warning shots near a UK-registered yacht in the English Channel. The incident occurred after the yacht drifted toward the military vessel while it was operating in the waterway.

BBC News has confirmed that the yacht moved toward the Russian frigate before the warning shots were fired. The encounter represents an unusual direct incident between Russian military forces and a British civilian vessel in the Channel.

hero.headline: SpaceX Acquires AI Startup for $60 Billion in All-Stock Deal
hero.body:
SpaceX has exercised an option to acquire Anysphere, the startup behind the AI-powered coding app Cursor, for $60 billion in an all-stock transaction, the company announced days after its record-breaking initial public offering.

The deal represents one of the largest technology acquisitions in recent years and expands SpaceX's artificial intelligence capabilities alongside its core aerospace business. By using stock rather than cash, SpaceX preserves its balance sheet while deploying its newly public equity as currency for growth.

SpaceX's IPO on Friday marked a historic milestone. The company began trading at $150 per share and climbed to $160 by market close, a gain of more than 19 percent. The offering valued SpaceX at $2.1 trillion, making it one of the world's most valuable companies. The company raised $75 billion from the public offering after nearly 25 years as a private enterprise.

The stock surge has dramatically increased Elon Musk's personal wealth. As SpaceX's majority shareholder controlling approximately 85 percent of voting shares, Musk became the world's first trillionaire, with his net worth reaching $1.1 trillion according to Forbes. His stake in Tesla, valued at around $300 billion, contributes to his overall fortune.

SpaceX's expansion into artificial intelligence reflects a broader strategy by Musk. The company told IPO investors it sees a $26 trillion addressable market in artificial intelligence. The Anysphere acquisition builds on SpaceX's existing AI division, xAI, which the company incorporated into its public structure. The technology could enhance autonomous rocket landing systems, satellite network operations, and future space exploration missions.

The company's rapid market ascent has positioned it ahead of several tech giants by valuation. SpaceX has surpassed Amazon and Meta in market capitalization, approaching Microsoft's standing.

However, SpaceX's financial picture presents complexities. Last year the company generated $18.7 billion in revenue while recording an operating loss of $4.3 billion. Analysts note that the company is burning cash on its AI infrastructure buildout, with xAI spending substantially on datacenters. Some market watchers have expressed caution about the company's significant valuation given its lack of profitability and concentration of control under Musk.

SpaceX's IPO included unconventional terms. Rather than offering a price range to investors, the company set a fixed pre-opening price of $135, with investor demand reportedly reaching four times oversubscription levels.

The acquisition reflects Musk's stated mission for SpaceX to "make humanity multiplanetary" and advance space exploration. Company president Gwynne Shotwell highlighted the company's accomplishments, noting that SpaceX launched a Falcon 9 rocket on IPO morning carrying 29 Starlink satellites to low-Earth orbit.

cards.headline: European Union Approves Trade Deal With United States
cards.teaser: After nearly a year of negotiations, EU lawmakers gave final approval to a trade agreement struck with President Trump in Scotland.
cards.body:
The European Parliament has given final approval to a tariff agreement with Donald Trump, nearly a year after it was initially proposed. The deal was negotiated in Turnberry, Scotland, and faced months of parliamentary deliberation before receiving support.

The approval came just days before a July 4 deadline, after which the U.S. threatened to impose increased tariffs. The Parliament approved the agreement with two main conditions attached.

cards.headline: General Motors Announces Defense Partnership With Lockheed Martin
cards.teaser: The automaker will collaborate with the defense contractor on weapons production, expanding GM's operations beyond consumer vehicles.
cards.body:
General Motors announced a new defense partnership with Lockheed Martin to collaborate on weapons production. The agreement marks a significant expansion of GM's business operations into the defense sector, where the automaker will supply weapons parts to the aerospace and defense contractor.

The partnership represents a strategic shift for GM as it diversifies its revenue streams beyond traditional automotive manufacturing. The collaboration will leverage GM's manufacturing capabilities to support Lockheed Martin's weapons systems production.

cards.headline: Gas Prices May Stay High Despite US-Iran Agreement
cards.teaser: Damaged infrastructure and transport risks could keep fuel costs elevated even after a preliminary deal between Washington and Tehran.
cards.body:
A preliminary agreement between the US and Iran may not immediately lower gas prices at the pump. While President Trump announced the deal would reopen the key Strait of Hormuz waterway, damaged oil production and distribution infrastructure in the Middle East will require time to repair and return to full capacity.

Transport routes remain uncertain, which could continue adding risk premiums to fuel costs. US gasoline has slipped below $4 per gallon for the first time since April, but analysts expect higher prices for gas, groceries, and flights to persist beyond the immediate crisis.

cards.headline: Pizza Hut Chain to Be Sold for $2.7 Billion
cards.teaser: The sale follows a prolonged period of difficulty for the pizza chain, which has faced mounting competition from rivals.
cards.body:
Yum! Brands, the parent company of KFC and Taco Bell, is selling Pizza Hut for $2.7 billion. The sale comes after the chain struggled with outdated stores and intensifying competition in the restaurant market.

In February, Yum! Brands announced it was exploring a sale of Pizza Hut and planned to close 250 U.S. locations. The transaction represents a significant shift for one of America's largest pizza chains as consumer preferences and market conditions have shifted.

cards.headline: Rivian Lays Off Hundreds of Workers
cards.teaser: The electric vehicle startup cut its workforce as the company faces ongoing financial pressures in the competitive EV market.
cards.body:
Electric vehicle startup Rivian has laid off hundreds of workers as part of a restructuring effort aimed at achieving profitability. The company recently began deliveries of its R2 vehicle and is working to scale operations more efficiently.

Rivian has also pushed back its profitability timeline to prioritize investments in autonomous driving technology. The layoffs reflect broader pressures facing EV manufacturers to control costs while advancing next-generation capabilities.

cards.headline: Micron Stock Rises Toward New High
cards.teaser: The memory chip manufacturer's shares climbed as Wall Street analysts predict further gains ahead of the company's earnings report.
cards.body:
Micron Technology's stock rose toward a new high as investors anticipated the company's upcoming earnings report. Wall Street analysts suggested the memory chip maker could see additional upside of 40 percent based on strong demand for memory products.

The stock has risen 811 percent during its recent run, driven by robust demand for memory chips used in data centers and AI applications. Analysts predict Micron's stock price could reach higher levels by late 2027, though some observers cautioned that memory stocks may be overbought.

hero.headline: Snap launches consumer AR glasses at $2,195
hero.body:
Snap has released its first consumer-focused augmented reality glasses, called Specs, priced at $2,195. The company announced the launch after years of development, marking its entry into the consumer AR market.

The new glasses represent a significant step for Snap, which previously offered developer-focused AR hardware. CEO Evan Spiegel has positioned the product as part of the company's vision for a future beyond smartphones, where digital information overlays the physical world through wearable devices.

The high price point places Specs well above typical consumer electronics, positioning them as a premium or early-adopter product rather than a mass-market device. The glasses will be available starting this fall, giving consumers several months to consider the purchase.

Snap has invested heavily in augmented reality technology over the past several years, developing filters and lenses for its mobile app while building hardware capabilities. The company views AR as a core part of its long-term strategy, even as it competes with larger tech companies like Meta and Apple in the wearable technology space.

The launch comes as the broader tech industry continues to explore AR and mixed reality hardware, with varying degrees of commercial success. Consumer adoption of AR glasses has remained limited due to factors including cost, design, and unclear use cases. Snap's entry into this market will test whether there is consumer appetite for AR glasses at this price level and whether the company can differentiate its offering in a competitive landscape.

cards.headline: Google releases Android 17 with new multitasking features
cards.teaser: Google has launched Android 17 and Wear OS 7, introducing multitasking tools, parental controls, and security features alongside AI updates for Pixel devices.
cards.body:
Google has rolled out Android 17 alongside Wear OS 7, delivering enhanced multitasking capabilities and expanded parental controls. The update also strengthens security tools across the mobile platform while improving smartwatch functionality through the new Wear OS version.

The release coincides with a Pixel Drop featuring Google's latest AI models. The update deepens Gemini integration throughout the Android ecosystem, embedding advanced AI features more extensively into the operating system.

cards.headline: SpaceX completes initial public offering
cards.teaser: SpaceX has gone public, marking a major milestone for the space company founded by Elon Musk after years of private operation.
cards.body:
SpaceX has completed its initial public offering, transitioning from private to public ownership. The company filed an S-1 registration document detailing its financials and business operations ahead of the IPO.

The public offering represents a significant shift for the space company, which has operated privately since its founding. The IPO creates potential winners among early investors and employees while subjecting the company to public market pressures and disclosure requirements.

cards.headline: Mobileye to launch robotaxi service in US city
cards.teaser: The Israeli tech company and Intel subsidiary said it will launch a robotaxi service in a US city in 2027.
cards.body:
Mobileye, an Intel subsidiary based in Israel, plans to launch its own robotaxi service in a U.S. city by 2027. This move positions the company to compete on both sides of the autonomous vehicle market—supplying technology to other manufacturers while operating its own fleet.

The expansion represents a significant strategic shift for Mobileye, allowing it to leverage its autonomous driving expertise while maintaining its existing role as a technology provider to the automotive industry.

cards.headline: Rivian cuts hundreds of jobs after R2 deliveries begin
cards.teaser: The electric vehicle maker said the cuts are part of restructuring efforts to reach profitability after recently pushing back its profitability timeline.
cards.body:
Rivian has laid off hundreds of workers as part of a restructuring initiative designed to help the company reach profitability. The cuts coincide with the automaker's launch of R2 vehicle deliveries.

The electric vehicle maker recently extended its timeline for achieving profitability in order to fund investments in autonomous driving technology. The company views the workforce reduction as a necessary step to streamline operations while pursuing financial sustainability.

cards.headline: India temporarily bans Telegram over exam fraud concerns
cards.teaser: The government has ordered a nationwide ban on Telegram until June 22 and required the app to disable its message-editing feature.
cards.body:
India has imposed a temporary nationwide ban on Telegram until June 22 due to concerns about exam fraud. The government has also required the messaging app to disable its message-editing feature as part of the restrictions.

The ban affects all users across India, blocking access to the encrypted messaging platform during this period. These measures are specifically aimed at preventing the use of Telegram in facilitating exam-related fraud.

cards.headline: SpaceX Dragon cargo capsule departs space station
cards.teaser: The cargo capsule undocked from the International Space Station and is returning to Earth with research materials.
cards.body:
A SpaceX Dragon cargo capsule undocked from the International Space Station and began its return trip to Earth. The spacecraft is carrying research materials, including bioprinted tissue and cancer treatment experiments.

NASA covered the departure as part of the 34th SpaceX resupply mission to the space station. The capsule completed its cargo delivery mission and will return scientific materials for analysis on Earth.

hero.headline: Sri Lanka defeat New Zealand at Women's World Cup
hero.body:
Sri Lanka beat defending champions New Zealand for the first time in Women's World Cup history, chasing down a target of 153 runs with two balls remaining. Kaushani Nuthyangana's four-wicket haul proved decisive in securing the upset victory for Sri Lanka.

The match marked a significant milestone for Sri Lankan women's cricket, ending New Zealand's previously unblemished record against them in the tournament. New Zealand, who entered the match as reigning World Cup champions, set a total of 153 runs for Sri Lanka to chase.

Nuthyangana's bowling performance anchored Sri Lanka's win, taking four wickets to restrict the defending champions to a chaseable total. Her figures proved crucial in keeping New Zealand's score within reach for the Sri Lankan batting lineup.

The successful chase came down to the final over, with Sri Lanka reaching the target with just two deliveries to spare. The narrow margin highlighted the competitive nature of the match, though Sri Lanka maintained composure in the closing stages to secure the historic result.

The victory represents a breakthrough moment for Sri Lanka in women's international cricket. Defeating the reigning champions marks a significant step forward for the program and could shift the dynamics of the tournament standings. For New Zealand, the loss ends their perfect record against Sri Lanka at the Women's World Cup and raises questions about their title defense.

cards.headline: France faces Senegal in World Cup 2026 match
cards.teaser: France takes on Senegal as part of a star-studded World Cup Day 6 slate featuring Messi, Mbappé, and Haaland.
cards.body:
France and Senegal face off in a World Cup 2026 match scheduled for 3pm EST/8pm BST. The fixture carries historical significance, as the teams previously met in the 2002 World Cup opener, which featured a notable performance from Senegalese forward El-Hadji Diouf.

The match is part of the tournament's sixth day of action. According to Othmane Sonoko, former prime minister and speaker of the Senegalese parliament, the contest holds deeper meaning beyond football, with the outcome representing Africa's strength regardless of which team prevails.

cards.headline: Jamie Smith misses England Test for daughter's birth as James Rew debuts
cards.teaser: England wicketkeeper Jamie Smith will miss the second Test against New Zealand following the birth of his daughter.
cards.body:
Jamie Smith will miss England's second Test against New Zealand following the birth of his daughter. James Rew will step into the wicketkeeper role as his replacement.

Rew's selection marks his Test debut for England. He becomes the third player making his debut in the match for the home side as England continues its series against New Zealand.

cards.headline: Rory McIlroy urges caution for US Open setup at Shinnecock Hills
cards.teaser: Rory McIlroy called on tournament organizers to ensure playing conditions at Shinnecock Hills remain fair during this week's US Open.
cards.body:
Rory McIlroy has called on tournament organizers to ensure conditions at this week's US Open do not spiral beyond acceptable limits. The event returns to Shinnecock Hills, a Long Island course with a troubled history of setup controversies.

McIlroy's warning reflects past disputes at the venue over course difficulty and playing conditions that have drawn criticism from players and officials alike.

cards.headline: John Tortorella will not return as Golden Knights coach
cards.teaser: The Vegas Golden Knights announced that John Tortorella will not return as head coach following the team's Stanley Cup Final loss.
cards.body:
John Tortorella will not continue as head coach of the Vegas Golden Knights. The team provided an update on its coaching staff after losing the 2026 NHL Stanley Cup Final.

Tortorella's departure follows the Golden Knights' finals defeat. The organization will now search for a new head coach as it looks to build on its recent playoff run.

cards.headline: Up to 15,000 England fans arrive in Dallas for World Cup opener
cards.teaser: England supporters are beginning to arrive in Dallas as the team prepares for its delayed 2026 World Cup campaign to begin.
cards.body:
England fans have had a longer wait than most national teams for their 2026 World Cup campaign to begin. Up to 15,000 supporters are now arriving in Dallas for the tournament opener, having had extra time to arrange their travel to the United States.

With the delayed start giving fans more opportunity to plan, supporters are gathering in the Texas city as England prepares to kick off their group stage campaign.

cards.headline: Austrian midfielder's rapid rise takes him from second tier to World Cup
cards.teaser: Motherwell attacking midfielder charts a quick ascent from Austrian second-division football to the World Cup stage.
cards.body:
A Motherwell attacking midfielder has completed a rapid rise from Austria's second tier to the World Cup. The player's journey has taken him from lower-division football to representing his country at the tournament's highest level.

The midfielder's breakout performances have attracted attention as he transitions from relative obscurity to international competition. His path illustrates one of the tournament's more unexpected player journeys.

hero.headline: Universal Content Productions and Universal International Studios Merge Into Universal Global Television
hero.teaser: Universal Content Productions and Universal International Studios are combining into a single studio unit.
hero.body:
The two production entities will now operate as Universal Global Television, consolidating operations under one banner. Beatrice Springborn, who currently serves as president of both Universal Content Productions and Universal International Studios, will lead the merged unit as president of Universal Global Television.

The restructuring brings together the domestic and international production arms of Universal's television business. The merger reflects ongoing consolidation in the television production industry as studios reorganize their operations.

cards.headline: ESPN Launches Womens Sports Sunday Programming Block
cards.teaser: ESPN will debut Womens Sports Sunday this weekend, dedicating prime Sunday night programming to womens athletics.
cards.body:
ESPN will debut Womens Sports Sunday this weekend, dedicating prime Sunday night programming to womens athletics. The Disney-backed sports network plans to air nine weeks of WNBA games and other womens sports competitions in time slots traditionally reserved for Major League Baseball.

The programming shift represents a significant investment in womens sports coverage by the network. ESPN executives view the move as an advancement in sports broadcasting, committing premium weekend evening hours to womens competitions rather than treating them as supplementary content.

Sunday nights have historically been a stronghold for baseball broadcasts on ESPN. The network is now repositioning those hours to feature womens basketball and other emerging womens leagues. The decision comes as multiple media companies have increased their womens sports offerings, including coverage of League One Volleyball matches.

The nine-week block will primarily feature WNBA games, with the professional womens basketball league receiving prominent placement in the sports calendar. ESPN's approach differs from competitors by concentrating womens sports into a dedicated weekly showcase rather than scattering games throughout the schedule.

The launch occurs during a period when womens athletics have gained increased viewership and commercial interest. ESPN's commitment of prime weekend programming hours signals confidence that womens sports can attract substantial audiences in traditionally high-value broadcast windows. The network has not announced plans beyond the initial nine-week run.

cards.headline: Louis C.K. Comedy Special Set for Netflix Release
cards.teaser: Netflix will release Louis C.K.'s new comedy special on June 30.
cards.body:
The special, titled Ridiculous, features material including a story about the comedian and his sisters placing their elderly father in a retirement home. In a trailer released by Netflix, C.K. jokes about the experience, saying his father was too old to prevent them from making the decision.

The special marks C.K.'s return to a major streaming platform. Netflix has scheduled the release for the end of June.

cards.headline: Fallout Season 2 Production Moves to Los Angeles
cards.teaser: The second season of Amazon's Fallout series has relocated filming from New York to Los Angeles.
cards.body:
The production shift brings the show to California during a period of reduced film and television activity in the state. Cast members expressed surprise at the changes in the local production landscape upon arriving in Los Angeles. The move coincides with the show's narrative transition to the Mojave Wasteland and New Vegas settings.

The creative team relocated the entire production operation to accommodate the new location requirements for Season 2. The series is adapting the video game franchise for television, and production continues in the Los Angeles area.

cards.headline: Millicent Simmonds to Write and Star in Crime Thriller Grace
cards.teaser: Actress Millicent Simmonds will co-write and lead the crime thriller Grace, the first film from Inevitable Studios.
cards.body:
Simmonds, known for roles in A Quiet Place and Pretty Lethal, is taking on dual responsibilities as co-writer and star. The project marks the inaugural production for Inevitable Studios, the film and television banner of Inevitable Foundation.

Inevitable Studios was founded by Richie Siegel and Marisa Torelli-Pedevska. The production company focuses on commercial film and television projects.

cards.headline: Black Diamond Comic Series Being Adapted as Folk Horror Film
cards.teaser: The folk horror comic book Black Diamond is being developed into a feature film by Fangoria Studios and Panick Studios.
cards.body:
Ernest Dickerson will direct and executive produce the adaptation. Dickerson has directed episodes of The Walking Dead and feature films including Tales from the Crypt: Demon Knight and Bones.

The project brings together two production companies specializing in horror content. Fangoria Studios and Panick Studios are collaborating on the adaptation of the comic series.

cards.headline: WIF and ReFrame Release Emmy Consideration Guide for Underrepresented Categories
cards.teaser: Women in Film and ReFrame published a guide highlighting women, nonbinary, and trans creators in Emmy categories with low gender diversity.
cards.body:
The Who to Watch TV FYC guide spotlights contributions from underrepresented creators in television series awards categories. Featured creators include Quinta Brunson for Abbott Elementary, Lucia Aniello and Jen Statsky for Hacks, and Jenny Han and Sarah Kucserka.

The guide focuses on categories that have historically shown less gender diversity in Emmy nominations. The organizations partnered to increase visibility for creators from underrepresented groups during the awards consideration period.

hero.headline: Senate Judiciary schedules confirmation hearing for attorney general nominee Todd Blanche
hero.teaser: The Senate Judiciary Committee set a confirmation hearing for Todd Blanche, nominated for attorney general.
hero.body:
The Senate Judiciary Committee scheduled a confirmation hearing for Todd Blanche, President Trump's nominee for attorney general. The hearing represents a key step in the confirmation process for the top Justice Department position.

Supporters hope Blanche can be confirmed before the August recess. The timeline would allow the nominee to take office before Congress breaks for its summer break.

cards.headline: Trump administration orders Anthropic to block foreign access to AI models
cards.teaser: The Trump administration issued an export control order to artificial intelligence company Anthropic, requiring it to block foreign nationals from accessing its.
cards.body:
Anthropic will disable its most advanced AI models, Fable 5 and Mythos 5, after receiving an export control directive from the U.S. government. The order requires the company to suspend access for all foreign nationals, citing national security concerns. Anthropic said it was not provided specific details about the security threat.

The government believes the models' safeguards can be bypassed and used to identify software vulnerabilities. AI researchers and cybersecurity leaders have raised concerns that this precedent could discourage American companies from developing defensive security tools, potentially weakening U.S. cyber defenses.

cards.headline: Former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem joins mining company advisory board
cards.teaser: Kristi Noem, now serving as Special Envoy for the Shield of the Americas, joined the advisory board of a Canadian mineral exploration firm.
cards.body:
Former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem joined the advisory board of Canadian mineral exploration firm NovaRed Mining, the company announced. Noem currently serves as Special Envoy for the Shield of the Americas in the Trump administration.

Noem will work in a strategic advisory role as the company seeks to acquire and advance critical mineral exploration projects. The appointment comes as she continues to hold her envoy position in the administration.

cards.headline: View hosts press Vice President Vance on racial equity policies
cards.teaser: Vice President Vance faced questions about Trump administration policies affecting Black Americans during an appearance on The View.
cards.body:
Vice President Vance appeared on The View, where hosts Whoopi Goldberg and Sunny Hostin pressed him on Trump administration policies. Goldberg and Hostin questioned Vance about the removal of Black history from sites around the country and the dismantling of majority-Black voting districts.

Goldberg asked Vance what Black people did to the administration that has allowed it to stigmatize people of color. The exchange highlighted ongoing debates over the administration's approach to racial equity and voting rights.

cards.headline: Jeffries asks Rubio to help Cape Verde goalkeeper's mother attend World Cup match
cards.teaser: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries urged the Secretary of State to ensure a visa for the mother of Cape Verde's goalkeeper.
cards.body:
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries urged Secretary of State Marco Rubio to help obtain a visa for the mother of Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha so she can attend her son's World Cup matches.

The request came after Cape Verde's impressive 0-0 draw against Spain in their World Cup opener. The 40-year-old Vozinha delivered a standout performance in goal, helping the debutant team hold the European champions in their Group H clash.

cards.headline: Vance defends Trump inflation comments during View appearance
cards.teaser: Vice President Vance responded to questions about President Trump's recent remarks on inflation during a television interview.
cards.body:
Vice President Vance appeared on The View on Tuesday to defend President Trump's recent statement about inflation. When co-host Ana Navarro pressed him on Trump's comment that he "loves the inflation," Vance attempted to reframe the remark, saying the president meant he loves that inflation will come down once the war ends.

The hosts challenged Vance on the administration's economic and social policies, questioning where Americans of color fit into the Trump vision and whether Vance serves as the president's interpreter on contentious statements.

cards.headline: Radio host criticizes White House standards after UFC event remarks
cards.teaser: Charlamagne tha God said standards of decency set by the Obamas no longer exist at the White House after derogatory remarks at a UFC event.
cards.body:
Radio host Charlamagne tha God said a standard of decency and class and poise and intelligence set by the Obamas does not exist anymore. The comments came after a fighter made derogatory remarks aimed at former first lady Michelle Obama during a White House UFC event.

Charlamagne questioned why supporters of the administration engage in such behavior. The incident drew criticism from commentators who contrasted current White House events with previous administrations.
